terms.meaning: how much of a profile a person can see or change.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup for family data
sections.what: Brings in the store library and the API client, and states the file's purpose: sharing access and managing profiles.
sections.why: Standard setup at the top of the file.

sections.name: FamilyMember
sections.title: Shape of one family member
sections.what: Describes one person: an ID, full name, relationship, optional access level, and whether they own the profile.
sections.why: Gives each family member the same shape.
sections.watch_out: The access level is free text, so the allowed values are not enforced here.

sections.name: FamilyState
sections.title: What the family store holds
sections.what: Lists the members, shared profiles, loading flag, and the actions to load profiles, add a member, and share access by email with a level.
sections.why: Keeps family state in one place.
sections.watch_out: Sharing is done by email address, so a typo could give access to the wrong person. The check for this is not visible here.

sections.name: useFamilyStore
sections.title: Family members and sharing actions
sections.what: Keeps the list of family members the user owns and the profiles other people have shared with them. It loads these lists from the server, adds a new family member, and sends a sharing invitation by email with a chosen access level.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps family data in one shared place so screens can show it and refresh it after changes. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The loading action only logs errors, so a screen can look empty without explaining why, while the add and share actions re-throw errors that the screen must catch.

summary: Holds the family members and shared profiles, plus the actions to load them, add a member and share access.
purpose: Lets users manage the people whose health records they look after, and share access with others.
why: Reason not stated in the code.
how: Starts with empty lists and loading off. The three actions are declared here. Their bodies are not in this packet, so exactly how each one works is unclear.
inputs: A name and relationship for a new member, and an email, access level and member ID for sharing.
outputs: The member and shared profile lists, and server requests.
risks: Sharing access by email could give health records to the wrong person. The sharing code is not visible here, so the check for this cannot be confirmed.
